subject: showing only centroid value (or mean of X and Y)?

messages.author: 452569198af8caee
messages.subject: showing only centroid value (or mean of X and Y)?
parts:
Hi!

I would like to know if there is a way in ggplot2 to plot the central
value of a group of points (or the mean on X and Y). With the data I
use, it get's to dense in some regions and since I have one factor
with 8 levels, it get's confusing with different colors (and worse
with different shapes).

I see that stat_summary seems to point out to what I would like to do,
but how to do it on both X and Y. I do not want to plot the original
data, but only the central value.

Here's a small example with qplot. I've used one factor with 2 levels,
and the other with 5.

val_x = runif(40,0,1)
val_y = rnorm(40,0,1)
fact1 = rep(1:2,each=20)
fact2 = rep(1:5,8)

test = qplot(val_x,val_y, shape=factor(fact1),colour=factor(fact2))

Thank you all for your help.

guillaume

messages.author: dc06d729e023580a
messages.subject: Re: showing only centroid value (or mean of X and Y)?
parts:
Hi Guillaume,

There's no way to do this purely in ggplot2, but it's pretty easy to
summarise the data yourself:

library(ggplot2)
df <- data.frame(
val_x = runif(40,0,1),
val_y = rnorm(40,0,1),
fact1 = factor(rep(1:2,each=20)),
fact2 = factor(rep(1:5,8)))

qplot(val_x,val_y, shape = fact1, colour = fact2, data = df)

mid <- ddply(df, c("fact1", "fact2"), summarise,
val_x = mean(val_x), val_y = mean(val_y))

qplot(val_x,val_y, shape = fact1, colour = fact2, data = df) +
geom_point(data = mid, size = 5)


Hadley

I think I need to do something pretty similar, but am running in
trouble and don't want to actually create another layer. Is there a
way to map the mean of a factor to the fill color of a boxplot? I've
got X and Y values I'm plotting as a boxplot, but then I'd like to use
the mean value of Z (for that group/factor) as a gradient fill on each
box to indicate the third value. Here's a simplistic representation of
what I'm trying, except I want the mean for hp:

library(ggplot2)
attach(mtcars)
p <- ggplot(mtcars, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))
p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = hp))

For my dataset, I think I need to actually take the mean explicitly,
otherwise the fill comes out blank for all factors that don't have
uniform values (missing data maybe?)

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 0c39e60ddb38622b
messages.subject: Re: showing only centroid value (or mean of X and Y)?
parts:
Hi:

You can probably use stat_something to do this more elegantly and
fiddle with the scales, but if you summarize the data before calling
ggplot(), you can sometimes save yourself some work.

I chose to get the average horsepower before going to ggplot(), setting the
result up as a factor with values rounded to two decimal places and named so
that I wouldn't have to resort to using scale_fill_* later on to change the legend title:

mtcars2 <- ddply(mtcars, .(cyl), transform, AvgHP = factor(round(mean(hp), 2)))
p <- ggplot(mtcars2, aes(factor(cyl), mpg))
p + geom_boxplot(aes(fill = AvgHP))

If you prefer the scale to be on a gradient instead, remove the factor() specification
in the definition of AvgHP in mtcars2, in which case the rounding isn't really
necessary. I prefer the version above because it displays the mean horsepower
per cylinder size in the graph, but your purposes may be different.

HTH,
Dennis
